profile.campus: Northlake, Cook County, Illinois (Microsoft Azure North Central US region)
profile.address: 601 Northwest Avenue, Northlake, Leyden Township, Cook County, Illinois, 60164
profile.reading:
This is Microsoft's Northlake, Illinois data center in the Chicago metro, one of the company's earliest large-scale, purpose-built cloud facilities. Data Center Knowledge reported in November 2007 that Microsoft agreed to occupy a speculative 441,000-square-foot building on a 12-acre property that developers Ascent Corp. and the Koman Group, with Turner Construction managing the project, had begun building without a tenant already lined up; the facility was expected to cost more than $500 million and came with 40 megawatts of power available at 5 cents per kilowatt-hour, backed by a dedicated on-site substation. At the time, Microsoft was simultaneously operating a 470,000-square-foot data center in Quincy, Washington and building a $550 million facility in San Antonio, part of a broader early-2000s buildout as the company raced to expand internet infrastructure to compete with Google and other web-services rivals. The Northlake facility now serves Microsoft's Azure North Central US region. A third-party data center aggregator has cited a roughly 120-megawatt capacity figure for the current Northlake campus, but this has not been confirmed by Microsoft directly and this registry treats it as an unverified lead rather than an operator-confirmed spec; Microsoft's own data center site publishes only aggregate worldwide statistics rather than per-facility details. Because the original 2007 reporting is now nearly two decades old, this registry treats the 441,000-square-foot, $500 million, 40MW figures as historical baseline facts about the facility's origin rather than a current specification, since Microsoft has not published whether or how the campus has since been expanded or upgraded.

ComEd, the Chicago-area electric utility, has cited large commercial and data center load growth in northeastern Illinois in its own distribution planning filings with the Illinois Commerce Commission, part of a broader pattern across Midwest utilities adjusting long-range forecasts to account for hyperscale campuses like Microsoft's Northlake facility alongside newer entrants to the region.

reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity for individual Azure data center campuses, including this Northlake facility in Cook County near Chicago. A third-party aggregator reports approximately 120 MW, but this figure is unverified against Microsoft's own disclosure. The campus is confirmed as part of the Azure North Central US region through public reporting of Microsoft's infrastructure expansion in Illinois.

If the 120 MW aggregator figure is accurate, it would represent roughly 3,000 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common density for cloud infrastructure mixing training and inference workloads. This would make the campus material to regional AI capacity but still modest compared to the largest hyperscaler builds announced elsewhere. The actual power envelope, IT load split, and cooling architecture remain unpublished.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only 6 operators publish power figures totaling 236 MW. This Northlake campus ranks seventh in the state by published capacity among the subset that disclose at all, but the majority of the state's mapped sites—including this one—operate under disclosure policies that treat facility-level specifications as confidential.
